title: The offset wheel on a geared carrier
description: From the fixed front view, determine how wheel P changes its own orientation and how its bearing on H travels around the common fixed center of S and H at the shown instant.
question: Drive A CW. Determine P (spin) and H (orbit) at the shown instant.

answer.explanation: Drive A CW. External mesh A/B (20/30 teeth) has fixed centers. A positive, B negative. The solid key makes B and H rotate together. B negative, H negative. S is locked to the frame. S held. External mesh S/I (24/18 teeth) uses spins relative to carrier H. S held, I negative. External mesh I/P (18/36 teeth) uses spins relative to carrier H. I negative, P negative. 24 × (S − H) + 18 × (I − H) = 0. 18 × (I − H) + 36 × (P − H) = 0. The requested motion is CCW / CCW (in listed output order).

options.label: A
options.explanation: This tuple matches the derived motions. The outer A-B mesh drives H counterclockwise through B. Seen from H, S turns clockwise. P follows S through two outer meshes at 24/36 of its relative speed. Adding H's larger counterclockwise speed gives P a counterclockwise frame spin.

options.label: B
options.explanation: P is CCW, while this choice gives CW. H is CCW, while this choice gives CW. Giving B the same sense as A carries a clockwise error into H and P. The labeled A-B contact is an external mesh and reverses the drive.

options.label: C
options.explanation: P is CCW, while this choice gives stationary. Perfect cancellation would hold with equal end wheels. The 36-tooth P gains only two thirds of the clockwise relative speed of the 24-tooth S, leaving a counterclockwise frame spin.

options.label: D
options.explanation: P is CCW, while this choice gives CW. This reports P's clockwise spin as seen by a rider on H. The frame observer must also include H's counterclockwise angular velocity.
